I haven't owned a Nintendo home console since the GameCube, I've primarily been a PC gamer and a handheld gamer. I've had all of Nintendo's handhelds since the Gameboy and a gaming PC for over 15 years.

I own a PS4 and I agree with most of what he says. I still haven't played a great game on it, but the Wii U's catalogue looks amazing. As a PC gamer I've also notice the effect that the console/PC convergence has had on PC games; it's made a lot of them mediocre ports. PC used to be the realm of the competitive FPS (because playing an FPS on a pad is a joke) but these days they're all average rehashes with very little potential for true competitive play.

So all the PC is left with is point-and-click strategy games: DoTA2, LoL et al. on the competitive side; EU4, CK2, Civ V, etc. on the more solo focused side. Everything else is an indie game (which are mostly quite good, to be fair, but not groundbreaking), or a shitty FPS focused on collecting hats and weapon skins. Most of the action games that could be truly great on the PC are being held back by the home console model/market. Where's my CS1.6 and Quake 3?

Not only has console convergence ruined the true home console market, it's also destroying the PC gaming market. =(

Why I still personally like Nintendo is that their games are fun months after I've bought them. They're still fresh and with my busy schedule it can be nice to just relax with creatively unique video games.

Yeah, Nintendo definitely is the only party I feel is doing console gaming correctly.
